title: Dependability stakeholder probe and runbook - 8 week experiment
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a working experiment plan: an 8-week rapid probe to validate a lightweight SLO adoption and cross-functional runbook pipeline for 6 lighthouse services. We want to test the minimal set of artifacts and rituals required to get feature teams to treat SLOs as a living contract: measurable, actionable, and tied to oncall flows.

Why this is different from larger SLO rollouts:
- Timeboxed (8 weeks) and intentionally opinionated: low ceremony, high observability.
- Focus on runbooks and handoffs rather than full governance.
- Measure adoption through a small set of signal+action metrics rather than headcount/process metrics.

Experiment goals (success criteria):
- Each lighthouse service has a 1-page SLO + 1 runbook + automated alerting wired into the SRE bridge.
- Error budget policy implemented for at least 4/6 services (enforced via alert suppression/annotations).
- Time-to-first-action metric: median time from alert firing to human-acknowledge < 5 minutes for P1s during business hours.
- Teams run at least one post-incident micro-retro within 72 hours for any P1 that consumes >33% of error budget.

Scope (what we will and won't do):
- In scope: 6 lighthouse services (combo of model-serving, routing, billing-proxy, cache-layer, console API, telemetry-ingest).
- Out of scope: org-wide SLO taxonomies, billing model changes, or SLA legal language.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Experiment lead (owner): Jordan Kim (eng-sre) - overall cadence, decisions, stakeholder syncs.
- Product liaisons: Priya Shah (hosted-api), Liam O'Connor (dedicated).
- Platform partner: Sofia Martinez (platform-engineering) - batching/infra knobs.
- Oncall owners: Ethan Reynolds (serving-runtime), Maya Gupta (observability).
- Exec sponsor: Rachel Park (VP SRE) - periodic check-ins.

Artifacts deliverable per service:
- 1-page SLO statement (service, hypothesis, metric, objective, window, customer-impact translation).
- Runbook (steps to diagnose, mitigation commands, temporary rollback actions, owners).
- Alert rules (thresholds + minutes + routing to SRE bridge).
- Error budget policy doc (annotation process, suppression matrix, escalation ladder).
- Post-incident micro-retro template pre-filled.

High-level timeline (8 weeks):
Week 0 (prep, pre-probe): align stakeholders, get permissions, set up central slack channel (#dep-probe).
Week 1: pick lighthouse services; run measurement baseline (current p50/p95/p99 latency & error rate).
Week 2: draft 1-page SLOs and share with product liaisons for translation into customer impact phrasing.
Week 3: implement alerting + test bridge routing (synthetic alerts + war-room dry run).
Week 4: create runbook drafts and run a 60-minute drill with service owners.
Week 5: enforce simple error budget policy for first service; record suppression/annotation flow.
Week 6: mid-experiment review; adjust thresholds based on false-positive analysis.
Week 7: execute a staged fault-injection test for 2 services (circuit breaker + degraded model fallback).
Week 8: harvest learnings, final retro, and decide next steps (scale, iterate, or kill).

Practical runbook template (one page, fillable):
- Symptom: what you see (example: "streaming generation latency > 2s P95 for 1 minute").
- Quickchecks (2 commands + expected outputs):
  - check pods: kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=gen -o wide  # expect >0 pod restarts
  - check metrics: curl -s http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count[1m])  # expect consistent per-replica counts
- Mitigation steps (ordered):
  1) Route traffic to canary/standby pool via router CLI (router swap --target standby).
  2) If model load issue: restart model-worker with graceful drain (workerctl restart --graceful).
  3) If downstream cache overloaded: apply short-term throttle (redisctl config set maxclients 200).
- Rollback action: revert last deploy (deployctl rollback --to=previous) and annotate release.
- Owner & backup: primary: Ethan Reynolds; backup: Priya Shah.
- Postmortem checklist: capture timeline, annotate error budget impact, record lessons and create 2 follow-ups.

Oncall and escalation flow (lightweight):
- Alerts route to SRE bridge channel + page primary oncall.
- Primary acknowledges within target (<5 min) or SRE bridge escalates to secondary after 6 min.
- If incident consumes >33% error budget OR lasts >30 minutes: exec pager to oncall lead + notify product liaison.
- Use annotation tag: eb_impacted=true to mark incidents that touch error budget.

Measurement plan and dashboards:
- Baseline reports: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rates, per-route token throughput (for model-serving).
- Error budget dashboard: remaining budget %, burn rate (1h & 24h).
- Time-to-first-action tracking: use bridge logs to compute ack times (store as metric slo_ack_seconds).
- False positive rate: alerts fired that did not lead to action within 10 minutes.

Hypotheses to test (each mapped to a thin metric):
1) Hypothesis: A 1-page SLO + runbook reduces time-to-first-action by 30% vs baseline. Metric: median ack time.
2) Hypothesis: Simple suppression + annotation reduces noisy paging by 40%. Metric: page count/day.
3) Hypothesis: Runbook drills increase confidence: measured by drill completion score (checklist pass rate).

Risk register (short):
- Risk: Alert fatigue from poorly-tuned thresholds. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, synthetic test days, and one-week tuning window.
- Risk: Resource contention for platform changes. Mitigation: platform reprioritization with exec sponsor and limited blast radius.
- Risk: Teams ignore annotations. Mitigation: require Product liaisons to sign-off on suppression policies.

Communications and rituals:
- Weekly 30-min sync (Wed 10am) with leads and product liaisons (focus: blockers, decisions).
- Bi-weekly stakeholder digest (email + Confluence short note) summarizing metrics and asks.
- #dep-probe slack for ad-hoc updates and dry-run notices.
- 1-hour final demo + retro with exec sponsor at end of week 8.

Decision points (what we will decide and when):
- End of Week 3: keep or adjust SLO targets after synthetic alerting test.
- End of Week 6: expand error budget policy to remaining services if >60% success.
- End of Week 8: approve expansion plan (scale to 12 services) or pause.

Operational playbooks to hand to teams (minimal viable set):
- SLO one-pager template (json + markdown).
- Runbook checklist + drill script.
- Alert tuning playbook (how to reduce flapping).
- Error budget annotation cheat-sheet.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Need to confirm which 6 lighthouse services (ask product liaisons to pick by Fri).
- Need bridge log access for ack-time metric; coordinate with observability infra.
- Establish synthetic traffic harness for model-serving (Sofia to propose options).
- Decide whether to use suppression via alertmanager or our internal router - pros/cons list needed.

Appendix: quick example 1-page SLO (model-serving-gen):
- Service: model-serving-gen (text-generation API).
- User facing intent: interactive generation for product chat and search.
- SLI: request latency P95 for first-token (ms) and 5xx rate per 5m window.
- Objective: P95 < 1200ms over 30d; 5xx < 0.5% over 30d.
- Error budget: 7.5% of availability over 30d.
- Actionable threshold: when 30m burn rate > 2x expected, page SRE bridge.

Notes on style and adoption:
- Keep documents short. The one-pager + runbook must be consumable in < 10 minutes.
- Prefer hands-on drills to long training docs.
- Focus on bridging product translation of impact: product liaisons must be able to explain customer impact in one sentence.

Next steps (immediate):
- Jordan: schedule kickoff and set up #dep-probe slack channel (today).
- Priya & Liam: pick lighthouse services (by Fri).
- Maya: grant bridge logs and create ack-time metric (by Tue next week).
- Sofia: draft synthetic harness proposal (by next Wed).

Document history and notes:
- Drafted as a lightweight experiment; expected to mutate rapidly.
- This file is the working single source-of-truth for the 8-week probe until final retro.
